#The DOM of a same-origin frame

Each document has its own JavaScript realm: an instance of the engine, compiled to Wasm, with its own heap. A browser's frames share a heap between documents of one origin, and pages rely on it: iframe.contentDocument.write(html), frame.contentWindow.someGlobal, parent.document, window.parent.foo(), rich-text editors, payment widgets, test harnesses. Wren gets the same result without sharing a heap, in two parts.

#Nodes: handles that name their document

The DOM lives on the browser's side; a wrapper in a realm is a handle. A handle now says which document it belongs to: 15 bits of its generation word are the document's tag (base.pool_insert_tagged, src/base/pool.odin). So a wrapper of a realm can hold a node of another document, and contentDocument and all that is reached from it are ordinary DOM wrappers of the caller's realm.

Every generated import trampoline hands its handle arguments to api_route (src/page/api_host.odin). A handle of another document moves the whole call to that document: Call.page is that page, Call.caller the one whose realm is calling, and the implementation does what it does for a page calling itself, so the frame's styles, layout, hooks and scripts follow. Imports of Document that name no node (createTextNode, title, write...) are preceded by a one-shot Frame_target.

What keeps a frame of another origin out:

  • a handle resolves in its own document only. The tag is in the slot's generation, so a handle given to the wrong document fails like a dead one, in any implementation, routed or not;
  • the document is looked up on each call, among the documents of the caller's tab, and its origin compared with the caller's (frames_may_reach, src/page/frames_access.odin). A frame gone, navigated to another origin, or sandboxed without allow-same-origin leaves handles that resolve to nothing;
  • a cross-origin frame's nodes never get a handle in another realm in the first place: contentDocument is null, contentWindow.document and parent.document throw a SecurityError.

document.domain has no setter in Wren, so it never widens an origin.

An insertion of a node of another document moves it first (DOM "adopt", Frame_adoptNode): a node has its handle in its document's pool, so this makes new nodes, with their listeners, and the wrappers of the realm that asked follow them. A custom element keeps its definition: its reactions run in the realm that defined it, adoptedCallback included. A wrapper another realm holds on the old node goes dead; a shadow root does not follow its host; a form control's typed value and the state of a media element stay behind. document.adoptNode and importNode across documents leave the node where it is until it is inserted, so ownerDocument tells the old document until then.

A wrapper belongs to a realm: the same element has one wrapper per realm that reached it, and a property set on one is not on the other. A method of a custom element of the frame's registry is not visible on the parent's wrapper of it. A MutationObserver follows other documents with a browser object in each.

Listeners may come from both realms. A listener added from another realm records a Foreign_Owner (its page, its instance), and runs in the realm that added it, a nested instance call. A script inserted in a frame runs in the frame's realm, wherever its element was made. All documents of a tab are on one thread, so a nested call needs no lock; the native stack check of src/wasm ends a recursion through realms as it ends one in a realm.

A document with a running call in it cannot be freed: page_close then takes it out of the tree at once and closes it when the call has returned (frames_close_later). The script goes on, in a document nobody can reach.

#Blank frames

A frame with no address (about:blank, the initial document) is a real document with a realm of its own, like any other, made on first need. Reached by another realm, it becomes a document that finished loading, shown in its frame (frames_make_live).

#Globals: a value bridge

frame.contentWindow.foo and parent.foo() go through native/js/odin/frames_bridge.odin and web_bridge.js. A request is bytes the browser carries from an instance to another (Frame_bridge, which checks the origin each time):

valuein the other realm
undefined, null, booleans, numbers, strings, bigintscopied
well-known symbolsby name; any other symbol is not carried
a DOM nodethat realm's wrapper of the node
a windowthat realm's WindowProxy, or its global
a built-in, an interface, their prototypesby name: that realm's own (what a window gives for them is the reader's)
any other object, a functiona Proxy forwarding get, set, has, delete, keys, descriptors, prototype, call, construct

An object coming home is itself. A realm that is gone answers undefined. Proxies are collected with FinalizationRegistry, which releases the object in its realm.

A listener or a handler that is a Proxy of another realm's function runs as a callback of that realm: what it throws is reported at that window's error event, and once that realm is gone it is not called.

What it is not is one heap:

  • since w.Array is the reader's Array, an object of another window reaches the reader's prototypes: x instanceof w.Promise and x.constructor === w.Object hold, and so does x instanceof Array, where a browser says false;
  • an object made with new w.Object is the caller's, so a listener made that way is the caller's too: what it throws goes to the caller's window (dom/events/EventListener-handleEvent-cross-realm.html);
  • a native function refuses a Proxy for one of its own objects: a typed array or a Blob of one realm passed to a native of another throws a TypeError. An Event to otherWindow.dispatchEvent is handled, and frameDocument.createRange() and getSelection() give the frame's own, which its Selection takes;
  • a cycle between two realms (a listener of one kept by the other) lives until one of them goes;
  • ECMAScript built-ins and interface objects read from another window are the caller's own: frame.contentWindow.Array === Array, and new frame.contentWindow.HTMLElement makes one of the caller's. A DOM wrapper's prototype is its realm's too: contentDocument.body instanceof HTMLElement is true, where a browser says false. navigator, screen, crypto and console of another window are the caller's as well.

A custom element class of one realm defined in the registry of another (frame.contentWindow.customElements.define(name, class extends HTMLElement {})) is not supported: its constructor would run in one realm for an element of another.

Rich-text editors reach their frame, but Wren has no editing of its own in contenteditable or designMode (typing, caret, execCommand): that limit is not about frames.

#Navigating a frame

A navigable keeps its session history across its documents (Navigable.session): navigation.entries(), back(), traverseTo() and reload() see them, keys and ids stay. The navigate event fires in the frame's document whoever starts the navigation (location of another window, window.open or a link or a form with a target, the src and srcdoc attributes), but for a navigation to another document started from another origin. The document that leaves gets beforeunload, then pagehide and unload, and starts no navigation while they run. A 204, a 205 or an attachment leaves the document as it is.

What is not there:

  • joint session history. Each frame has its own: history.back() in the tab does not go back in a frame, a traversal moves one frame, and a push in a frame does not prune another's forward entries. The browser's back button leaves the tab's document;
  • a Window kept from the initial about:blank. HTML keeps the Window when a frame goes from its initial about:blank to a document of the same origin. Here every document has an instance of its own, so what a script put on a blank frame's window (frame.contentWindow.navigation.onnavigate = ..., window[0].foo = ...) goes with that document;
  • precommitHandler of NavigateEvent.intercept().

#Cost

A page without frames pays two comparisons per handle argument of an import call, and one load per call. The tag replaces bits of the generation: pool_get compares what it compared. A slot reused 65536 times is retired rather than wrapped.
